Share Share Share Tension is mounting at Fisher, a farming community near Ettukrom in the Abuakwa North Municipality of the Eastern Region, following the alleged destruction of several acres of a rubber plantation by some Chinese investors.
Community leaders allege that the investors, together with their Ghanaian mining counterparts and armed military personnel, forcefully entered the plantation, destroyed several acres of rubber trees and drove peasant farmers from their farms.
They further claim that the farmers have been threatened against returning to the plantation.
Citi News has gathered that the invasion of the rubber plantation, which previously belonged to Nawara Mining Company, follows the alleged takeover of the company’s concessions and operations by the Chinese investors and their Ghanaian counterparts.
However, the traditional rulers of Ettukrom, who are the custodians of the concession, maintain that the lease granted to Nawara Mining Company for the rubber plantation has expired, making the land due for a return to the traditional authority.
Addressing a press conference on the matter, the Chief of Ettukrom, Barima Ettu Adomako III, called on President John Dramani Mahama, the Ministry of the Interior, National Security and the Ghana Police Service to intervene immediately to prevent the situation from escalating.
“I’m calling on the President to intervene in the matter. There is an allegation that Ibrahim Mahama, the President’s brother, has taken over the concession. However, no documents have been presented to support the claim, making it difficult for me to believe the information.
“If Ibrahim Mahama is indeed involved, we need to engage in dialogue. But if he is not involved, we demand that the encroachers leave the land,” he said.
